claims.text: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won an unprecedented fourth term as president of Brazil on Sunday.
Lula da Silva defeated Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro.
Flávio Bolsonaro finished first in the first round of Brazil's presidential election.
Lula da Silva was imprisoned from 2018 to 2019 on corruption charges that were later overturned.
Lula da Silva previously served as president of Brazil between 2003 and 2011.
Leftist federal lawmaker Erika Hilton called Lula da Silva 'a statesman, a giant' during the vote count in São Paulo.
Bolsonaro's Liberal Party and allied parties could control over 280 seats in Brazil's lower house and up to 50 seats in the Senate.
With over 78% of votes counted in Brazil's runoff, Lula da Silva led with 51.21% against Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.79%, according to Reuters live coverage.
Voting was extended nationwide in Brazil by two hours following an order by Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin.
Jair Bolsonaro led Lula da Silva by more than 2.2 million votes in the first round of the presidential election.
More than 33 million of Brazil's nearly 160 million voters did not participate in the first round of the presidential election.
With nearly 99% of votes counted, 80-year-old Lula da Silva received 51.75% of the vote compared to 45-year-old Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.25%.
Pro-Bolsonaro congressman Nikolas Ferreira told journalists, 'Either we win. Or we win. You've been warned.'
Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup.
A court in Bahia ordered the arrest of a top transportation official in Salvador over allegations of reducing election day public buses.
Half a million first-time voters are eligible to vote in Israel's general election, and around 70,000 Israelis are reportedly flying in from abroad to cast ballots.
Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff, leads the centrist Yashar party in Israel.
Gadi Eisenkot's son was killed during the Gaza War.
A pro-Netanyahu TV debate participant used a racist slur referring to Gadi Eisenkot as a Moroccan 'monkey'.
A survey indicates that over 70% of Jewish Israelis support establishing a state commission of inquiry into the October 7, 2023 attacks.
Arab citizens make up around one-fifth of Israel's population.
Billionaire American investor Bill Ackman stated that Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich should not serve in Israel's next government due to reputational damage.
Bill Ackman and his wife Neri Oxman own a 5 percent stake in the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.
Donald Trump publicly endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu for Prime Minister of Israel.
Itamar Ben-Gvir's Jewish Power party is projected to win around 10 seats in the Israeli parliament, while Bezalel Smotrich's Religious Zionism is projected to win 8 seats.
Gadi Eisenkot and other Israeli opposition party leaders ruled out forming a coalition government with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Serbian leader Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat in the parliamentary election, stating the Student List won between 135 and 140 seats while his party won 105.
A poll sample by CeSID-IPSPS projected the Student List would secure 138 seats and the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) would take 104 seats in parliament.
Voter turnout reached 67.6% by 7pm local time in Serbia, marking the highest level since the breakup of Yugoslavia in 1992.
The collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad in November 2024 killed 16 people and sparked nationwide student-led protests.
Aleksandar Vučić resigned from the presidency last month to trigger snap parliamentary elections.
Aleksandar Vučić has dominated Serbian politics as prime minister or president since 2014.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen congratulated the Student List on its election victory.
The Student List fielded 250 candidates led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanović.
Aleksandar Vučić blamed independent media, unnamed European nations, and an 'American deep state' for his election defeat.
Election monitors reported suspected voting irregularities in Serbia, including ballot photographing and attempted vote-buying.
Preliminary election commission figures showed turnout reached 64.9% by 18:00 local time in Serbia.
Serbian riot police cordoned off the election commission headquarters in central Belgrade on election day.
Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned home on Sunday after more than 10 months in exile.
María Corina Machado fled Venezuela secretly on a speedboat in December 2025 to receive the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway.
In January 2026, US forces seized President Nicolás Maduro, who is now jailed in New York on drug, weapon, and torture charges.
The Trump administration backed Delcy Rodríguez as interim president of Venezuela following Nicolás Maduro's capture.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that conditions allowing Machado's safe return were the direct result of US-supported reconciliation talks.
María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela by taking a private plane from Panama to Colombia and crossing overland.
US President Donald Trump said of Machado's return, 'I don't know anything about it' and added, 'we're doing really well in Venezuela.'
Machado's Vente Venezuela movement launched an app to collect voter registration data from Venezuelans living abroad.
María Corina Machado is 59 years old.
Donald Trump announced an oil deal with Venezuela in August 2026 that he called 'the biggest oil deal in world history'.
María Corina Machado called for new presidential elections in Venezuela to be conducted by July 2027.
Supporters greeted María Corina Machado during a church service in Barquisimeto, Lara state.
Marine Le Pen officially launched her French presidential campaign on Sunday before 8,500 supporters in Orléans.
More than 2,000 people were arrested across France during nationwide protests on October 17.
Approximately 3,000 police officers were deployed in Orléans ahead of Marine Le Pen's rally to prevent anti-far-right unrest.
The French Senate will debate a proposed 'vandals pay' bill allowing non-damaging protesters to be held liable for up to €10,000 in property damages.
Marine Le Pen stated at her Orléans rally, 'Vandals will pay and if it takes their whole life to pay, then they will spend their whole life paying.'
Leftist lawmaker Éric Coquerel warned that the 'vandals pay' law 'would mean the end of street demonstrations' in France.
France's Ministry of the Interior reported that 410,000 people demonstrated nationwide on Saturday, including 110,000 in Paris.
French authorities deployed over 70,000 police officers and gendarmes nationwide for Saturday's demonstrations.
Cultural institutions including the Louvre, Musée d'Orsay, and Art Basel Paris closed or cancelled events due to Saturday's protests.
More than 1,300 arrests were made during nationwide protests in France on Saturday.
French trade unions estimated that 800,000 people participated in Saturday's cost-of-living and school condition protests.
The Interior Ministry reported 53 police officers were injured in clashes across France on Saturday.
A 20-year-old protester in Toulouse had several fingers severed when an explosive went off near him during protests.
Around 13,000 people attended a peaceful counter-rally against the National Rally in Orléans on Saturday.
Donald Trump launched an anti-Muslim attack against Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed during the US midterm campaign.
Abdul El-Sayed is competing against Republican Mike Rogers for a US Senate seat in Michigan.
Donald Trump encouraged crowd members at a Michigan campaign rally to compliment rapper Nicki Minaj's appearance.
Barack Obama joked at a campaign rally that Donald Trump 'has got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.'
Donald Trump claimed at a rally that the US-Canada trade war would end soon because Canada is 'willing to give us anything at this moment.'
Donald Trump called Abdul El-Sayed a 'Jihadist Member of the Muslim Brotherhood' on Truth Social and alleged he wants to impose Sharia law in the US.
Trump claimed at a Port Huron rally that Abdul El-Sayed's mother worked for an organization that funded Osama bin Laden and Al-Qaeda.
Barack Obama campaigned in Detroit alongside Democratic candidates Abdul El-Sayed and Jocelyn Benson.
Barack Obama told an Ohio rally that Americans face higher living costs due to 'an unnecessary war that nobody asked for and nobody voted for.'
Political ad spending for the 2026 US midterm election cycle has surpassed $10 billion and is projected to reach $11.6 billion.
Republicans spent $233 million on broadcast television ads across nine close Senate races last month, compared to $121 million spent by Democrats.
Combined political ad spending and reservations in Texas's Senate race between James Talarico and Ken Paxton surpassed $500 million.
Elon Musk donated $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund and $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC.
Political ad spending in Ohio's Senate race reached over $450 million.
Republican groups have committed nearly $114 million for advertising in Maine's Senate race, compared to about $81 million committed by Democrats.
